title: Regular Expressions
description: Flavor-aware regular-expression reference covering literals, character classes, anchors, quantifiers, groups, alternation, captures, lookarounds, backreferences, Unicode, replacement, engine differences, performance, ReDoS prevention, debugging, and testing.

subtopics.title: Literals, Character Classes & Escapes
subtopics.description: Most characters match themselves; metacharacters need escaping. Character classes match one character from a set, with flavor-dependent shorthand and Unicode behavior.

rows: Newline behavior is normal class behavior

callouts.title: Escape Twice in String Literals
callouts.text: A programming-language string parser may consume escapes before the regex engine sees them. Prefer regex literals or raw strings where the language supports them.

subtopics.title: Anchors, Boundaries & Match Modes
subtopics.description: Anchors assert positions rather than consuming characters. Start/end behavior changes with multiline modes; full-input APIs or absolute anchors are safer for validation.

callouts.title: Search and Full Match Differ
callouts.text: A search succeeds when any substring matches. Validators should use a full-match API or correctly anchored pattern and account for trailing line terminators and multiline settings.

subtopics.title: Quantifiers, Greedy & Lazy Matching
subtopics.description: Quantifiers repeat the preceding atom. Greedy forms take as much as possible then backtrack; lazy forms take as little as possible but can still backtrack extensively.

callouts.title: Lazy Does Not Mean Efficient
callouts.text: Constrain what can match and use bounded quantifiers when the domain has limits. A lazy wildcard may still test many candidate endpoints.

subtopics.title: Capturing, Non-Capturing & Named Groups
subtopics.description: Groups control precedence and quantify subexpressions. Capture only values the caller needs; use named groups for stable readable extraction where supported.

callouts.title: Capture Numbering Is Fragile
callouts.text: Adding an earlier capturing group renumbers later captures. Prefer non-capturing groups for structure and named groups for outputs.

subtopics.title: Alternation & Precedence
subtopics.description: Alternation has low precedence and engines commonly try alternatives left to right. Group alternatives and put specific branches before broad prefixes when flavor behavior requires it.

callouts.title: Anchor the Whole Alternation
callouts.text: ^cat|dog$ means starts with cat OR ends with dog, not a full match of either word. Group before applying shared anchors or quantifiers.

subtopics.title: Lookarounds & Backreferences
subtopics.description: Lookarounds assert surrounding text without consuming it; backreferences require the same text captured earlier. Availability and lookbehind restrictions vary widely.

callouts.title: Backreferences Leave Regular-Language Territory
callouts.text: They can be expensive and are unsupported by RE2-style engines. Use ordinary parsing or sets when checking repeated arbitrary values at scale.

subtopics.title: Unicode Properties & Normalization
subtopics.description: Unicode-aware engines can match script, category, or letter/number properties, but syntax and flags vary. Normalize only when domain semantics permit it.

callouts.title: Case-Insensitive Matching Is Not Locale Logic
callouts.text: Unicode case folding, locale-specific casing, normalization, code points, and grapheme clusters are distinct. Use dedicated Unicode libraries for user-facing text segmentation and identifiers with security requirements.

subtopics.title: Backtracking, RE2-Style & POSIX Flavors
subtopics.description: Regex syntax and matching policy differ among JavaScript, PCRE, Java, .NET, Python, Rust/RE2-style engines, POSIX tools, and database implementations.

rows: Different escapes/capture syntax and leftmost-longest semantics

callouts.title: Name the Target Flavor
callouts.text: A pattern is incomplete documentation without engine, version, flags, host-language escaping, and match API. Test it in the actual runtime.

subtopics.title: Replacement, Extraction & Splitting
subtopics.description: Replacement templates have their own syntax for numbered/named captures and literal currency/backslash characters. Callback replacement is safest for conditional or transformed output.

callouts.title: Zero-Length Matches Affect Global Operations
callouts.text: Engines must advance after empty matches, but split/replace iteration semantics differ. Include empty and boundary cases in tests.

subtopics.title: Catastrophic Backtracking & ReDoS
subtopics.description: Nested ambiguous repetition and overlapping alternatives can create exponential work in backtracking engines, especially when failure occurs near the end of attacker-controlled input.

codeBlocks.code:
Risk shapes:
  repeated group containing repetition
  alternatives sharing long prefixes inside repetition
  unbounded wildcard followed by many possible suffixes

Mitigate:
  bound input and quantifiers
  remove ambiguity / factor prefixes
  use atomic/possessive constructs where supported
  choose a linear-time engine for untrusted patterns/text

callouts.title: A Timeout Is Defense in Depth
callouts.text: Some runtimes cannot interrupt a running regex safely. Prevent dangerous patterns, cap input, isolate work where necessary, and benchmark adversarial near-matches.

subtopics.title: When to Use a Parser Instead
subtopics.description: Regex excels at local lexical patterns and extraction. Recursive nesting, escaped delimiters, full programming languages, HTML/XML, and complex structured formats generally need a parser.

codeBlocks.code:
Regex: log line prefix, identifier, bounded token, simple rewrite
Parser: JSON, URL semantics, HTML DOM, SQL, nested expressions, CSV quoting
Hybrid: regex tokenizer → parser/state machine → domain validation

callouts.title: Validation Often Needs Domain Logic
callouts.text: A syntactically valid date, email-shaped string, path, or identifier may still violate calendars, deliverability, authorization, normalization, or business constraints.

subtopics.title: Debugging, Tests & Checklist
subtopics.description: Use free-spacing/comments where supported, name subpatterns, test positive/negative boundaries and adversarial inputs, and measure actual engine behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
Test: empty, shortest, longest, adjacent, multiline, Unicode, malformed
Near miss: long valid prefix + invalid final character
Flags: case, multiline, dotall, global/sticky, Unicode
API: search vs full-match vs find-all vs replace
Property: generated valid strings match; mutations fail as intended

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Declare flavor and flags, anchor validators, group alternation, minimize captures, bound repetition/input, handle Unicode deliberately, avoid parsing structured languages, test replacements and zero-length cases, and benchmark adversarial near-matches.
